body.summary: Member calls with built-in method names are kept on receivers proven user objects by a type or a new expression: class fields and constructor parameter properties typed with a user class or defaulted/initialised with new X(), this.x = new X() assignments, typed or new-defaulted parameters, const/let and var locals, and values asserted to a user class (as / satisfies / <T>), looking through parentheses and !. Class field proofs are per class (class, class expression and abstract class are boundaries), and `this` proves a receiver only where it is the class instance (class method, field initialiser, or an arrow inside one). Built-in classes, unions, arrays, primitives and untyped values never prove one. Mutation-checked.
